## Overview

My research sits at the intersection of quantum sensing, precision instrumentation, and
scientific software. I work with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond — atom-sized
quantum sensors that can detect magnetic fields, electric fields, and temperature with
nanoscale spatial resolution at room temperature. My goal is to push the limits of what
these sensors can image and measure, and to build the instrumentation and software
infrastructure that makes advanced quantum sensing experiments accessible and reproducible.

---

## Quantum Sensing

NV centers in diamond are among the most versatile solid-state quantum sensors available
today. Their long spin coherence times at room temperature, combined with all-optical
initialization and readout, make them ideal for precision sensing of magnetic and electric
fields, strain, and temperature. My work focuses on optically detected magnetic resonance
(ODMR) and electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy of NV ensembles, characterizing
spin coherence properties (T₁, T₂, T₂*) in CVD-grown diamond samples, and understanding
the role of nitrogen concentration and charge-state conversion in determining sensor
performance. Alongside magnetometry, I also work on bio-sensing with NV centers and on
ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) and spin-wave generation and detection in thin-film
magnetic heterostructures.

---

## Quantum Magnetic Imaging

I build and operate wide-field NV-diamond quantum sensing microscopes for magnetic
imaging at the microscale. By illuminating a diamond with a dense NV ensemble under a
wide-field fluorescence microscope, it is possible to reconstruct full two-dimensional
magnetic field maps with diffraction-limited spatial resolution over a large field of view —
simultaneously and without scanning.

Recent work has applied this platform to imaging magnetic domain structures in
ferromagnetic van der Waals materials and skyrmions in magnetic thin films with chiral
overlayers, demonstrating the capability of NV microscopy to resolve nanoscale magnetic
textures in novel materials at ambient conditions. An ongoing direction is microwave-free
quantum magnetic imaging using high-density NV ensembles, which eliminates the need for
resonant microwave driving and extends the technique to magnetically sensitive samples.

---

## Neuromorphic Quantum Imaging

A central theme of my current research is high-speed quantum magnetic imaging using
neuromorphic, event-based sensors. Event cameras — inspired by the biological retina —
report pixel-level brightness changes asynchronously, with microsecond temporal resolution
and very high dynamic range, rather than capturing full frames at a fixed rate. Integrating
event cameras with wide-field NV microscopy opens a path to information-efficient,
high-speed imaging of dynamic magnetic processes that would otherwise be inaccessible
with conventional sCMOS or CCD detectors.

---

## Quantum Control

Realizing the full sensitivity potential of NV ensembles requires precise quantum control
of the spin states. I work on pulse engineering for NV systems, including dynamical
decoupling sequences that extend spin coherence, and real-time experiment control using
the Quantum Machines OPX platform. Accurate microwave pulse calibration, phase control,
and synchronization with optical excitation and detection are critical to all pulsed
measurements — from Rabi oscillations and Ramsey spectroscopy to more advanced
quantum control protocols.

---

## Scientific Software

I develop open-source software for NV-center experiments, with a focus on modularity
and instrument abstraction. The [NV Control Framework](https://github.com/AmandeepQLab/NV-Control-Framework)
is a Python/PyQt6 application for automated control of confocal and wide-field NV
experiments, integrating drivers for cameras, signal generators, pulse streamers, and
positioning stages into a single coherent interface. Reproducible, well-documented
experimental software is an integral part of how I do science.

---

## Nanofabrication

Diamond processing and surface preparation are essential to NV-sensing performance.
I am a licensed user of the HUJI Center for Nanoscience and Nanotechnology, with
hands-on experience in atomic force microscopy (AFM) and magnetic force microscopy (MFM),
Elionix electron-beam lithography (including PMMA nanolayers on glass/silicon),
Microtech LW405B laser writing, and ellipsometry — used for characterizing and preparing
diamond surfaces and thin-film heterostructures for quantum sensing experiments.

---

## Previous Research

Before transitioning to NV-center quantum sensing, I worked in NMR quantum information
processing. During my PhD at IISER Mohali (2013–2019, supervisors: Prof. Kavita Dorai and
Prof. Arvind) and a subsequent postdoc at SUSTech, Shenzhen (2019–2021, group of
Prof. Dawei Lu), I developed and ran NMR experiments for entanglement detection and
classification, quantum process tomography, non-local correlation detection, and
experimental quantum principal component analysis. This work resulted in nine
peer-reviewed publications in journals including *Physical Review Letters*,
*Physical Review A*, and *European Physical Journal D*.
